title: Abruzzo and Conero
subtitle: Montepulciano's best wines
objectives: Describe Montepulciano d'Abruzzo and its DOCG

steps.title: Abruzzo
steps.body: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC is huge, from cheap and cheerful to serious. Montepulciano d'Abruzzo Colline Teramane became DOCG in 2003, requiring at least 90% Montepulciano and longer ageing. Producers like Valentini and Emidio Pepe have shown how long-lived it can be.

steps.title: Conero
steps.body: Monte Conero is a limestone headland on the Adriatic, near Ancona in the Marche. Rosso Cònero DOC must be at least 85% Montepulciano. Conero DOCG, the Riserva, since 2004, requires two years of ageing. Sea breezes and limestone give structured, fresh, dark wines.

steps.prompt: Which wines are based on Montepulciano?
steps.explanation: Vino Nobile is Sangiovese from the Tuscan town.

steps.title: Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo
steps.body: Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo is a deep cherry-pink rosé from Montepulciano, its own DOC since 2010. Cerasuolo means cherry-like. Short skin contact with this deeply coloured grape gives a darker, fuller rosé than most, with cherry, strawberry and a savoury edge.

steps.explanation: Its deep cherry colour gives Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo its name.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Colline Teramane is Abruzzo's DOCG Montepulciano
Conero, by the sea, makes structured Montepulciano
Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo is a deep cherry rosé
